chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But over those who take him as a guardian.
And who take others besides Allah as allies.
And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardians/allies

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) elucidation that Satan’s dominion is conditional upon human choice, specifically over those who voluntarily align with him as masters. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of free will (*ikhtiyar*), affirming that true believers (*mu'minun*) remain under divine protection unless they actively surrender their agency to evil. The narration serves as a foundational proof for the concept of *wilayah* and the spiritual hierarchy of guidance versus misguidance.
